blocks.text: Step-by-step prompting writes an instruction as an explicit, numbered sequence of actions the model should carry out in order, first do this, then do that, distinct from chain of thought, covered earlier, which elicits the model own internal reasoning trace rather than specifying a fixed procedure.

This topic covers how step-by-step prompting differs from chain of thought, how to break a complex instruction into a clear ordered sequence, and the common pitfall of steps that are either too vague or too finely broken down.
1. What Step-by-Step Prompting Means

blocks.alt: Building on plan and solve prompting, step-by-step prompting specifies an ordered procedure to follow

blocks.text: Step-by-step prompting writes the instruction itself as an explicit sequence, step one, do this, step two, do that, rather than describing the desired outcome in a single sentence and leaving the actual procedure implicit.
2. Step-by-Step vs Chain of Thought

blocks.alt: Chain of thought elicits the model own reasoning, step-by-step specifies a procedure to follow

blocks.text: Chain of thought, covered in an earlier topic, asks the model to reveal its own reasoning process toward an answer it has to work out, step-by-step prompting instead hands the model an explicit procedure you have already designed, and asks it to execute that procedure faithfully, these are genuinely different techniques solving different problems.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Technique","What It Asks the Model to Do"],"rows":[["Chain of thought","Work out its own reasoning toward an answer"],["Step-by-step prompting","Follow a procedure you have already specified"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Breaking a Complex Instruction Into an Ordered Sequence

blocks.alt: One dense, unordered instruction is compared against numbered, ordered steps

blocks.text: A dense instruction like "clean up this document by removing the headers, converting bullets to numbers, and adding a title" bundles three distinct actions into one sentence, breaking it into an explicit numbered sequence removes any ambiguity about what order those actions should actually happen in.

code.content:
prompt = """
Process this document by following these steps in order:
1. Remove all section headers.
2. Convert bulleted lists to numbered lists.
3. Add a single title summarizing the document content.
"""

blocks.text: 4. Why Explicit Ordering Reduces Ambiguity

blocks.alt: Step 1 removes headers, step 2 converts bullets to numbers, step 3 adds a title

blocks.text: When steps genuinely need to happen in a specific order, converting bullets to numbers before adding a title might produce a different result than doing it after, stating that order explicitly removes any chance the model executes the actions in an unintended sequence.
5. Numbering Steps vs Just Listing Them

blocks.alt: An unnumbered, loosely ordered list is compared against an explicitly numbered list

blocks.text: A bulleted list without numbers can still imply some ordering, but numbering each step explicitly removes any doubt, this small formatting choice, numbers instead of bullets, makes sequential intent unambiguous.
6. When Steps Depend on Previous Step Outputs

blocks.alt: A later step depending on an earlier step output means the sequence must be followed in order

blocks.text: Some step sequences have a genuine dependency, a later step needs the actual result of an earlier one, calculate a subtotal in step one, then apply a discount to that subtotal in step two, in these cases, explicit step-by-step prompting is not just a clarity nicety, it is functionally necessary for a correct result.

blocks.title: This dependency is exactly where step-by-step prompting earns its value
blocks.content: When steps are genuinely independent of each other, ordering barely matters, when a later step depends on an earlier one output, explicit sequential instructions become functionally important, not just stylistically clearer.

blocks.text: 7. Common Pitfall, Too Many or Too Vague Steps

blocks.alt: Too many overly granular steps are compared against appropriately sized steps

blocks.text: Breaking a task into so many tiny steps that the instruction becomes unwieldy defeats the purpose, each step should represent one genuinely meaningful action, granular enough to be unambiguous, but not so fragmented that the sequence becomes tedious to follow or read.
8. Step-by-Step Prompting in Reusable Templates

A fixed procedure that applies to every call, exactly the kind of stable content that belongs in a reusable template, covered in an earlier topic, is a natural fit for step-by-step prompting, the ordered steps rarely need to change even as the specific input content varies from call to call.
9. Combining With Other Techniques

Step-by-step prompting combines naturally with structured prompting, covered earlier in this module, labeled sections for role and constraints alongside a clearly numbered procedure, and with output format specifications, describing exactly how the result of the final step should be presented.
Worked Example

A developer asks a model to "clean up this messy meeting transcript" as a single dense instruction, results vary inconsistently, sometimes fixing grammar first, sometimes reorganizing structure first, producing different quality outcomes each time.

Rewriting the same request as an explicit numbered sequence, first fix obvious transcription errors, then remove filler words, then organize into clearly speaker labeled paragraphs, produces consistent, correctly ordered results across many different transcripts, since the procedure itself is now fully specified rather than left implicit.
Common Mistakes

items: Bundling several distinct actions into one dense sentence instead of an explicit numbered sequence
Breaking a task into so many overly granular steps that the instruction becomes unwieldy
Confusing step-by-step prompting, a specified procedure, with chain of thought, the model own elicited reasoning
Leaving step order ambiguous for a sequence where a later step genuinely depends on an earlier step result

blocks.text: Practice

Take a task you have prompted as one dense instruction before, break it into an explicit numbered sequence of steps, and test whether the numbered version produces more consistent results across several different inputs.
Key Takeaway

Step-by-step prompting writes an instruction as an explicit, ordered sequence of actions to follow, distinct from chain of thought reasoning, and it earns its value specifically when a task involves genuinely sequential dependencies or enough distinct actions that a single dense sentence would leave the intended order ambiguous.
